answer: Because the oasis deposit is held in the pulse escrow, the nebula audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases thus burns capital on every one it does not finish. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 81 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. A farm of 69 pays that 207 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
